news.title: 'Nobody is angry with him' - Barcelona sporting director Deco insists club never imposed surgery on Frenkie de Jong after World Cup knee injury
news.lede: Barcelona sporting director Deco has addressed the long-standing speculation surrounding Frenkie de Jong's fitness and the internal handling of the midfielder's recent injury woes. Speaking candidly about the Dutch international's recovery process, the club official dismissed rumours of friction between the player and the board regarding medical decisions. Clarifying the surgery controversy The situation surrounding De Jong became a major talking point following the World Cup, where the midfielder represented the Netherlands despite nursing a significant knee issue. It was later revealed that he had suffered a lateral internal ligament tear, a diagnosis the club only confirmed after De Jong returned from a 13-day post-tournament holiday in Ibiza.

news.title: After sparking widespread anger, FIFA paves the way to repeat 2026 World Cup 'novelty' at the 2030 edition
news.lede: It appears that FIFA is unconcerned by what happened at the 2026 World Cup, with a press report stating that football's world governing body is planning to repeat something that caused major controversy at the 2030 World Cup, which will be held in Morocco, Spain and Portugal. FIFA brought in two mandatory drinks breaks of around three minutes each for every match at the World Cup, the first around the 22nd minute and the second around the 67th. Plenty of coaches and players complained that the stoppages turned matches into four quarters rather than two halves, killing the momentum of whichever side was on top or pushing forward. Officials suggested the breaks could hand weaker national teams a chance to catch their breath and regroup, much like a "time-out" in some other sports.

news.title: Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks to stay in 2030
news.lede: Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters. Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made. Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup include a provision for broadcasters to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication the controversial ­stoppages will be retained. A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.

news.title: Spain’s World Cup winner Juan Mata announces retirement from professional football
news.lede: Home » Sports » Football » Spain’s World Cup winner Juan Mata announces retirement from professional football. New Delhi, Nov 18 (SocialNews.XYZ) Spain’s 2010 FIFA World Cup winner Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing the curtain down on a career spanning nearly two decades and featuring some of the biggest honours in club and international football. The former Chelsea and Manchester United midfielder made the announcement on Wednesday through a video message recorded at Juventud Estadio in Oviedo, where he first began playing organised football at the age of 10. Mata, who represented clubs across Spain, England, Turkey, Japan and Australia, retires with an impressive collection of silverware, including the FIFA World Cup, UEFA European Championship, UEFA Champions League and two UEFA Europa League titles.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß takes jab at Julian Nagelsmann’s handling of World Cup
news.lede: Uli Hoeneß is already making it pretty clear what he expects from Jürgen Klopp’s Germany tenure, and there might be a little side-eye directed toward the previous regime in the process. Hoeneß believes Klopp will bring discipline, hunger, and a renewed sense of urgency to the national team, while taking a subtle shot at Julian Nagelsmann’s approach to team culture, particularly the infamous family-oriented World Cup camp. ”I don’t think there will be another family outing with player wives and children under Jürgen. I believe he will bring discipline and hunger back.

news.title: Netflix in $2bn World Cup bidding war that could change sport forever
news.lede: Given the tournament is regarded to be the biggest across sport, rights to cover matches are incredibly lucrative for broadcasters. FOX Sports are the existing holders and transmitted fixtures during this summer's tournament as Spain went all the way to win their second title. However, there could be a landmark change in coverage of the sport in the US ahead of the next World Cup. Streaming giants Netflix are interested in bidding, say The Guardian, and the rights could be worth between $1.5bn (£1.1bn) and $2bn (£1.5bn).

news.title: FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027: Brazil Countdown
news.lede: The road to the FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027 is gathering momentum. For the first time, South America will host the world’s biggest women’s football tournament, placing Brazil at the centre of a historic moment for the game. In our monthly countdown, we’ll follow the key developments shaping the tournament and its wider impact on women’s football, bringing you stories, updates and insights from Brazil and beyond through the perspective of our exclusive correspondent in Brazil, Elena Mueller. The tournament will take place from 24 June to 25 July 2027, across eight Host Cities, with 32 national teams competing in 64 matches.

news.title: Football: Soccer-US women's coach Hayes leaning on veterans for World Cup qualifier
news.lede: Nov 18 (Reuters) - US women's national ⁠team coach Emma Hayes will rely on veteran players to guide the team during their World Cup qualifying campaign ⁠this month, with a coveted direct ticket to Brazil on the line. Hayes on Wednesday named her 23-player ‌squad for the upcoming CONCACAF W Championship, where aquarter-final win against El Salvador on November 27 would secure their qualification to next year’s World Cup. Leading the Americans is the dynamic attacking trio of TrinityRodman, Mallory Swanson and Sophia Wilson, with midfielder Sam Coffey also returning to the fold after missing the ​previous two windows through injury. "Qualifying for a major tournament, first and foremost, I'll ⁠be leaning on our experienced players,” Hayes said ⁠on a media call.
